2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland Receives New Suspension Lift, PHEVs Get the NACS Port and More Potent AC
66 photos
Photo: Toyota Motor Corporation
The 2027 Toyota RAV4 comes with enhancements, but unfortunately, they're not available on every model; the Woodland and PHEVs get all the attention. One major detail isn’t missing: MSRPs.
The Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC), the world’s largest and most valuable automaker, just announced its financial results for the second quarter, which ended September 30, 2026, and it almost got a positive result: consolidated global vehicle deliveries were 4.758 million units, missing the mark by just 25k vehicles compared to last year.
In North America, they were even closer to a positive quarter: 1.53 million units, and the slide was just 3k examples. However, the region’s operating income without interest rate swaps increased by 266.1 billion yen ($1.67 billion). As for Toyota Motor North America, or TMNA , its local division, the company is very busy focusing on the 2027 model year changeover, especially for the namesake Toyota brand.
We have recently seen the details regarding the 2027 Toyota Tundra, which gains a refreshed exterior, an upgraded TRD Pro suspension, “significant enhancements” in towing technology, and, most importantly, access to the new Trailhunter package. But Toyota also announced the 2027 Sequoia, Crown Signia, Camry, Corolla Cross, Grand Highlander with the new Woodland Edition, or the trio of electrics previously.
Well, now it’s time for the main attraction: Toyota’s regular best-seller is still trying to catch up to its previous generation, and so far, this year it has conceded the throne of the compact crossover SUV class to the Honda CR-V, but the RAV4 is not giving up the crown without a fight. So, the 2027 RAV4 “remains Toyota’s benchmark small SUV, offering a fully electrified lineup in a choice of HEV and PHEV powertrains, available FWD or AWD, and a broad range of grades tailored to different driving lifestyles.”
The second model year of the sixth generation comes with “two notable updates for the new model year: a revised suspension for the RAV4 Woodland grade, pushing ground clearance up to 9.1 inches, and the addition of a NACS port for all PHEV grades.” The 2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland is arguably the bigger news: the off-road-focused grade receives new suspension components, including new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, raising the ground clearance from 8.1 inches on all the other trim levels except the GR Sport, which has it even lower to a new standard of 9.1 inches.
The Woodland also gains redesigned all-weather floor and cargo mats, while all PHEV models now have a NACS port and DC fast charging (Level 3) capability, with the charging port now situated on the driver’s side on all PHEVs, and the new onboard AC charger has a speed of 11 kW on all PHEV grades. Additionally, all trim levels gain a backup camera washer, while the AWD models now have Multi-Terrain Select with Rock & Dirt and Mud & Sand modes.
The Multi-Terrain Select replaces Trail mode and Snow mode can be accessed now via the drive mode select switch alongside Normal, Eco, Sport, and Custom, plus the Remote Connect trial has been increased from one to no less than five years for all grades. MSRPs kick off at $32,300 for the LE FWD grade – as opposed to $31,900 for the 2026 model year. The PHEVs now kick off at $42,100 for the SE, which was $41,500 before. So, what do you think – yay or nay?
